topics.title: Finding Domain and Range
topics.text:
Ok so I was asked to find the domain and range of $f(x)=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x+1}+3}$ and I decided to get rid of the nasty radicals in the denominator by multiplying by the conjugate, $\sqrt{x+1}-3$. So now we have $\dfrac{\sqrt{x+1}-3}{x-8}$. So I thought, "well since $x-8\neq0$ obviously $8$ can't be in the domain" but when I plugged it into the original expression I got a valid, defined output $\big{(}\dfrac{1}{6}\big{)}$. So what did I do? :o



Also anyone else get $\big{(}0,\dfrac{1}{3}\big{]}$ for the range?
